requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

Documentation comments participate in structural hashes. Ordinary comments
are excluded. Included comment prose is grouped as inner or outer documentation;
delimiters are excluded, and consecutive comments of one group hash as one word
sequence. Reflowing that prose preserves its hash; changing its words changes it.
Attributes attached to an item participate in that item's hash.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately check `requirements.sdk.sources.rust.fingerprints`. The tests below are in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs` or `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs`.

**Mapping of obligations to tests**

- **Word-based hashing under `structural_hash`.**
  - `prose_words_are_encoded_separately` asserts that `/// ab cd` and `/// abcd` hash differently.
  - `string_literals_hash_as_words` asserts that extra whitespace inside a string literal keeps the hash, and that removing the space changes it.
  - `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` covers the Rust case with `/// two   words` against `/// twowords`.
- **SHA-256 digest.** The same test asserts that each fingerprint is a 64-character hex string. The encoding is deliberately unspecified, so a known-answer digest test isn't possible. The length and format check is the most the text allows.
- **Fingerprint scheme.**
  - `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline` asserts that `languages::Rust.fingerprint_scheme()` is `"rust-structural-v1"`.
  - The same test asserts that `OutlineContent::fingerprint_scheme()` on loaded content equals the language's scheme, so loaded contents retain it.
- **Doc comments participate.**
  - `editing_a_doc_comment_word_changes_the_hash` and `hashes_skip_whitespace_and_plain_comments_but_not_doc_comments` change a doc word (`Doc.` to `Docs.`, `count` to `total`) and assert that the hash changes.
  - `reflowing_doc_comments_keeps_the_hash` asserts that dropping a word (`a c` against `a b`) or reordering (`b a`) changes the hash.
- **Ordinary comments excluded.**
  - `hashes_skip_whitespace_and_plain_comments_but_not_doc_comments` changes a leading `//` comment (`a.b` to `c.d`) and keeps the hash.
  - `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` edits a `/* note */` comment inside a function body and keeps the hash.
- **Delimiters excluded and consecutive comments hashed as one sequence.**
  - `reflowing_doc_comments_keeps_the_hash` shows that `/// a`, `/// b` equals `/// a b`, equals `///   a`, `///`, `///   b  `, equals `/** a\n * b\n */`.
  - `reflowing_inner_and_block_doc_comments_keeps_the_hash` covers inner `//!` and `/*! */`, and shows that `/**` block comments equal `///` lines.
- **Inner and outer groups.** `inner_and_outer_doc_comments_hash_in_separate_groups` shows that moving a word between an inner and an outer group changes the module hash. It also shows that splitting words across comments within one group keeps the hash.
- **Attached attributes participate.** `hashes_skip_whitespace_and_plain_comments_but_not_doc_comments` replaces `#[inline]` with `#[cold]` and asserts that the hash changes.
- **Context.** `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` and the `hashes_skip_whitespace_…` test also check reformatting invariance, body edits and identity-hash behavior.

**Conclusion**

Each obligation in the requirement text has a test that exercises it and asserts the outcome. I found no unaddressed input class, boundary or failure case, and no {fixme} acknowledgments are involved.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Documentation comments participate in structural hashes. Ordinary comments
are excluded. Included comment prose is grouped as inner or outer documentation;
delimiters are excluded, and consecutive comments of one group hash as one word
sequence. Reflowing that prose preserves its hash; changing its words changes it.
Attributes attached to an item participate in that item's hash.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
